passages.text: The soul is like a crystal in the sunshine over which a thick black cloth has been thrown, so that however brightly the sun may shine the crystal can never reflect it.
passages.note: Inner light hidden, not lost, by wrongdoing

passages.text: Let humility be always at work, like the bee at the honeycomb, or all will be lost. But, remember, the bee leaves its hive to fly in search of flowers and the soul should sometimes cease thinking of itself to rise in meditation on the grandeur and majesty of its God.

I believe we shall never learn to know ourselves except by endeavouring to know God, for, beholding His greatness we are struck by our own baseness, His purity shows our foulness, and by meditating on His humility we find how very far we are from being humble.
passages.note: Self-knowledge found by looking beyond oneself

passages.text: Do not trouble yourselves, my daughters, with cares which do not concern you.
passages.note: Worrying over things that are not yours to carry
